name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 28, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:01 p.m., on March 28, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 9, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs (arrived at 5:30 p.m.)
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

City Council Minutes  1  March 28, 2017
 CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property: 26836 Oso Parkway, Mission
  Viejo Agency Negotiators; Dennis Wilberg, William Curley, and Elaine Lister:
  Negotiating Party: Jamboree Housing Under Negotiations Terms for Previously
  Approved Refinancing.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, the Council gave direction
to the City's negotiator and for item CS2, the City Council received information. There was no
reportable action on either topic.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Southern California Edison Annual Reliability Report

  The City Council received the report from District Manager Dirk McConnell and Local
  Public Affairs Manager Karalee Darnell.

ADDITION OF A LATE ARISING ITEM RELATING TO THE REQUEST FOR A ONE-
TIME EXEMPTION TO THE "NO ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE CONSUMPTION"
REGULATION AT CITY FACILITIES FOR A MEMORIAL SERVICE

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that staff would like to add an item to the Consent Calendar
(item 6A) pursuant to Government Code Section 54954.2(b2) to allow that alcohol be served at
the Celebration of Life for Mark "Ziggy" Wilczynski on April 8, 2017. Adding items to the agenda
requires a two-thirds vote and two findings: (1) that there is a need to take immediate action, and
(2) that the matter arose subsequent to the posting of the agenda.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to declare a
need to consider this matter which arose subsequent to the posting of the Agenda, and to affirm
that the matter must be considered before the next meeting with the recommendation that it be
addressed tonight.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  2  March 28, 2017
 AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following expressed frustration that Congresswoman Mimi Walters has not held a Town Hall
Meeting with Mission Viejo residents: Vivian Frerichs, M.V.; Brooke Leys-Campeau, M.V.;
Deborah Cunningham-Skurnick, M.V.; Lauren Austin, M.V.; Judy Fike, M.V.; Liz Rickett, M.V.;
and Eric Nelson, Dana Point.

Lynne Goldsmith, M.V.: stated that her business, PLAYlive Nation, is situated in such a way that
patrons have trouble finding it. She asked that the City's sign regulations be changed to allow for
additional signage on a temporary basis to help drive up business.

Bill Ernisse, M.V.: discussed the March 25 Wounded Warriors amputee softball game and
Veterans Resource Fair as well as the Working Wardrobes fundraiser and 5K walk along the Oso
Creek Trail. He thanked the City Council for their help with these events and for all that they do
for the City of Mission Viejo.

Julie Collier: introduced herself as a representative of Congressman Darrell Isaa and
invited residents to reach out to the Congressman’s office to learn more about upcoming Federal
legislation that might affect the community.

Victoria Avery, M.V.: thanked the City Council and staff for their service to the community. She
expressed disappointment at the person(s) who posted fliers about high-density housing at the
shopping center across the street from city hall and she asked that the City to find out who posted
them.

Sharon Campbell, M.V.: on behalf of Assemblyman Bill Brough, she thanked the City Council
and staff for their significant support with the Wounded Warrior amputee softball game and the
Veterans Resource Fair.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: expressed concern with the treatment that the Mayor and Council are receiving
from members of the public in regards to Mimi Walters.

Dan Avery, M.V.: stated he doesn't agree with anyone in national politics but the Council Members
in Mission Viejo are people with integrity.

Rudy Padrol, M.V.: announced that he is 67 days sober and on a mission to continue raising
awareness about drug addiction and overdose. He has teamed up with Jodi Barber and Dr. Headrick
to promote the movies Overtaken and Kids From The Other Side to help inspire youth to make
their teen years drug and alcohol free.

City Council Minutes  3  March 28, 2017
 CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated March 3, 2017 in the Amount of $606,456.80

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated March 10, 2017 in the Amount of $3,409,997.03

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Cox Communications State Franchise Certificate and P.E.G. Fee Ordinance

  Adopted Ordinance 17-323 Reauthorizing Ordinance 07-249, as Amended for Currency,
  Pursuant to California Public Utilities Code Section 5870 (5870N) (Division 2.5) and
  Readopting all Previous Findings, Analysis and Legislative History for Ordinance 07-249.

6.  Requests for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  Regulation at City facilities for Community Events and Programs

  Approved the request for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage
  Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

6A.  Requests for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  Regulation at City facilities for a Memorial Service (item added subsequent to the
  posting of the agenda – see page 2)

  Approved the request for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage
  Consumption" Regulation at City facilities for the Celebration of Life for Mark
City Council Minutes  4  March 28, 2017
   "Ziggy" Wilczynski at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center on Saturday,
  April 8, 2017.

7.  City of Mission Viejo Updated Local Implementation Plan and Water Quality
  Improvement Plan

  Adopted Resolution 17-10 Approving the City of Mission Viejo's Submittal of the Updated
  City of Mission Viejo Local Implementation Plan to the San Diego Regional Water Quality
  Control Board, Approving the County of Orange's Submittal of the Water Quality
  Improvement Plan to the San Diego Regional Water Quality Control Board, and
  Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Incorporate Further Amendments into the
  Local Implementation Plan and Water Quality Improvement Plan.

8.  2016 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 838)-
  Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date
  of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City; and (4) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

OLD BUSINESS

9.  Core Area Vision Plan

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Andrew Watkins and Sean O’Malley with SWA and Joan Isaacson with Kearns & West
  presented the results of the Vision Plan process and an outline of possible enhancements
  to the civic core.

  The following expressed concern with the Vision Plan methods, the concept of housing in
  the civic core as well as traffic and potential re-zoning: Michael Cline, M.V.; Cathy
  Schlicht, M.V.; and Gail Reavis, M.V.

  The following commended the Council for undertaking the Vision Plan process and
  expressed support for enhancements to the civic core: Robert David Breton, M.V.; Larry
  Ryan, M.V.; Sharon Campbell, M.V.; Andrew Steen, M.V.; Rita Tayenaka, M.V.; Jeff
  Creer, M.V.; and Eric Chastain, M.V.

  The following discussed the potential merits of upgrades to the City’s core area but
  expressed concern with the possibility of commercial and/or housing over retail space,
City Council Minutes  5  March 28, 2017
   large parking structures, traffic issues, etc.: Sheila Edmond, M.V.; Raydene South, M.V.;
  Millie Summerlin, M.V.; Eamon Kane, M.V.; Joe Tully, M.V.; and Matt Trudell, M.V.

  The City received 12 written statements in opposition to high density housing and 13
  written comments in favor of various improvement levels to the area.

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1)
  approve the Core Area Vision Plan report, as recommended by the Planning and
  Transportation Commission; and (2) authorize staff to: (i) Entered into a MOU with Santa
  Margarita Water District (A17-07) to conduct a feasibility Study, not to exceed $50,000,
  to repurpose the water treatment facility located off La Paz Road and within the Core Area
  (see Attachment); (ii) Enter into an Agreement with Fuscoe Engineering (A17-08) for
  Constraints Map (property boundaries and encumbrances) and Project Coordination for an
  amount not to exceed $16,000 (See Attachment); (iii) Public Services Department staff
  coordination for creek repair and clean-up (Costs to be determined); (iv) Further refine and
  enter into an Agreement with SWA to prepare Conceptual Plan and illustrative renderings
  for Core Area Creek Improvements (current proposal at $95,000 – final agreement to return
  to City Council for approval); (v) Enter into an Agreement with Consultant (A17-09) for
  Property Owner outreach, coordination/ negotiation regarding the creek improvements/
  catalyst project (estimate $12,000); (vi) Enter into Agreement with Fuscoe Engineering
  (A17-10) for follow up work, including Concept Plan Review of SWA plan related to
  constraints and civil engineering design (grading, drainage, utilities etc.) and Cost Estimate
  Support ($8,000) (see Attachment); (vii) Enter into an Agreement with Consultant (A17-
  11) to identify Funding Mechanisms and related follow through (estimate $6,000); and
  (viii) Follow-up with SCAG regarding revised scope for the $120,000 grant award for Core
  Area plan.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

10.  Marguerite Aquatics Complex Renovation (CIP 14325) - Utility Stub-Outs

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to (1) approve
  Contract Amendment No.2 to Construct One Corp. in an amount not to exceed $27,923.33
  for Utility Stub-Out construction items; (2) adopt Resolution 17-11 Amending the CIP
  14325 Marguerite Aquatics Complex Rehabilitation Project By Adding a Cash
  Contribution and Appropriation for the Utility Stub-Outs As Part of the Project Scope; and
  (3) authorized the mayor to sign the Nadadores Conditional Agreement (A17-13) for a Gift
  Contribution.

City Council Minutes  6  March 28, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour 9:17 p.m., Mayor Bucknum declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:31
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs noted that during his Council Comments on March 14, he
  inadvertently referred to Aliso Viejo Elementary School when talking about an anti-
  Semitism issue. He said he meant to say Los Alisos Middle School and asked that the
  Minutes be amended to reflect the correct school name.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
  the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of March 14, 2017, as amended.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

11.  Council Chamber and MVTV Studio Audio Visual & Broadcast Upgrade Project

  Director of Community Relations/City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  approve entering into agreement with and issuance of purchase order to Western Audio
  Visual (A17-14) in an amount not to exceed $613,361.19 plus a 10% contingency for
  services including equipment design and implementation of audio visual, voting and room
  control.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  7  March 28, 2017
 NEW BUSINESS

12.  Supplemental Health Account for Retired Employees (SHARE) Plan Administration

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-12 Adopting the ICMA Retirement Corporation's VantageCare Retirement
  Health Savings Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

14.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

15.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Battalion Chief John Abel announced that there were 35 graduates at the March 15 fire
  academy ceremony and one of those new firefighters will be stationed in Mission
  Viejo. He also noted that OCFA is beginning early planning discussions for the remodel
  of Fire Station 9 in town. Lastly, Chief Abel reminded the Council and residents that OCFA
  is looking for volunteers to help distribute and install free smoke alarms to the community
  on Saturday, April 8, 2017, from 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

City Council Minutes  8  March 28, 2017
 Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his attendance at the Orange County Sheriff’s Department
Medal of Valor award luncheon. He said it was outstanding to listen to and see the officers and
non-sworn personnel who dedicate their lives to helping others live safer lives. He noted that some
of Mission Viejo’s own officers were honored and the City is very proud of them. He also attended
the Wounded Warrior amputee softball game and Veterans Resource Fair and he congratulated
Council Member Raths for doing a great job as the announcer. Council Member Goodell further
discussed his attendance at the Orange County Association of Realtors annual Economic Forecast
event where he learned a new word, miserabilism, which means gloomy pessimism or negativity.
He said those that have been out spreading false information on high-density housing are
miserabilists. Council Member Goodell thanked everyone who has been involved in the Vision
Plan process and those that came out for the discussion at tonight’s meeting.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley said that she is glad she is not a miserabalist but rather, she is an optimist
and likes to do good. She discussed her attendance at recent events including the Capistrano Valley
High School basketball team awards recognition where the Mayor presented certificates to the
team and coaches for winning CIF; the ribbon cutting for a new travel agency, Trip Designs, and
the Orange County Sheriff’s Department Medal of Valor recognitions. Council Member Kelley
recounted that it was truly heartwarming to listen to the stories of the courage and lifesaving that
goes on every day and she was glad for the opportunity to recognize Mission Viejo Deputies Chris
Quenault, Steve Hortz, and Travis Krudwig. She also discussed the energy update she heard at the
South Orange County Economic Coalition and her attendance at the Wounded Warrior amputee
softball game and Veterans Resource Fair. Council Member Kelley thanked Senator Pat Bates and
Assemblyman Bill Brough for hosting those events. She further congratulated the Mission Viejo
Activities Committee on their 50th year of service and noted that the volunteers of the MVAC do
so many good things for the community. Council Member Kelley invited residents to Bunny Days
on April 15, Earth Day/Arbor Day on April 22, and Arts Alive on April 29 and 30. In closing,
Council Member Kelley paid tribute to “Mr. Mission Viejo” and Hometown Hero Mark “Ziggy”
Wilczynski who recently passed away. She said Ziggy was the City’s unofficial historian and his
service had a huge impact on Mission Viejo.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths announced that the Rotary will hold its annual Texas Hold ‘Em fundraiser
on June 10, 2017. Tickets will be $60 and half the money will go to the charity of the attendee’s
choice. He discussed the presentation by Southern California Edison earlier in the meeting and
stated that he didn’t get much out of it and would appreciate a better presentation next time.
Council Member Raths thanked Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander and I.T.
Department staff David Le and David Meyer for their help with his presentation to the Mission
Viejo Chamber of Commerce on the MV Life smartphone app and he thanked staff member Karen
Wylie for being so engaged with the business community and the Chamber of Commerce. He
discussed the business owner who spoke earlier in the evening regarding business signage and he

City Council Minutes  9  March 28, 2017
 asked staff to look into an occasional sign regulation waiver to help businesses thrive. Council
Member Raths mentioned the continuing litigation with the former Mayor for her RV parking and
he stressed that he’d like to see the matter concluded. In closing, he said that the anti-Mimi Walters
folks should stop attacking Mayor Bucknum and instead, focus their efforts on contacting Mimi
Walters directly to ask for a meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs agreed with Council Member Raths on the earlier presentation by Edison
which was way too technical for most people to understand. He thanked the City Manager and
Director of Library and Cultural Services Genesis Hansen for helping him when he discovered that
his passport had expired just two days before a trip to Germany. He shared the funny story of this
4:00 a.m. drive to the Federal building in Los Angeles where he spent 7-8 hours waiting for his
passport, followed by a rush hour drive home before tonight’s meeting. In the end, he got his
passport and said he is excited to see his son who has been stationed in Germany for a year. Mayor
Pro Tem Sachs discussed his attendance at the Orange County Fire Authority graduation ceremony
and noted that he would highly recommend it to others. At the end of the ceremony, the training
center tower was lit on fire and it was spectacular to see the graduates jump into their turnout gear
and run off to put the fire out.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum announced that she attended the Mission Hospital student auxiliary Bollywood
event. She said she has a heart for the youth that are getting involved in the community and it was
a delightful evening. She also discussed her attendance at a south county contract cities working
group with Supervisor Bartlett and Sheriff Hutchins which was focused on the Sheriff’s contract.
She said that the collaborative group is looking at ways to save money and she noted that the group
looks to City Manager Wilberg as an expert on the history of these contracts.

City Manager Wilberg noted that in a follow-up meeting today, he learned that the current estimate
has gone down by almost $500,000 so the City is making progress.

Mayor Bucknum discussed her attendance at recent events including the Sheriff’s Department
Medal of Valor luncheon, a Nowruz New Year celebration and the Wounded Warriors amputee
softball game and Veterans Resource Fair. She thanked residents Eileen and Victor Gonzalez who
originally brought the Wounded Warriors to Mission Viejo. Mayor Bucknum addressed the public
comments earlier and reiterated that the City has a long history of being open and welcoming to
listen to the concerns of the public. But, she said, listening doesn’t guarantee that the City can
accomplish what people are requesting. She noted that the City has already hosted a Town Hall
meeting with Congresswoman Walters in March 2016 and last December, the City Council
extended an invitation to Congresswoman Walters and many other state and federal officials to
host their events. Mayor Bucknum expressed her appreciation to Council Member Raths for the
support he showed tonight and she thanked her colleagues for their decorum in doing the business
of Mission Viejo. In closing, Mayor Bucknum shared that Jadon Pollard, a well-known and loved
trainer at the Montanoso Recreation Center, has passed away and information on his services will
be announced at the next meeting.
City Council Minutes  10  March 28, 2017
 STAFF REPORTS (continued)

City Attorney Bill Curley responded to Council Member Raths’ comments on the ongoing
litigation with former Council Member Schlicht. He said that the City has extended the invitation
to settlement but has not heard back. Instead, the City received new motions which have delayed
the proceedings into May. Mr. Curley noted that the City is trying to come to a proper and prompt
solution but things are not always in the City’s control.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:21 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Mark "Ziggy" Wilczynski and Jadon
Pollard, to Tuesday, April 11, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of April 25, 2017

City Council Minutes  11  March 28, 2017
